subtopics.title: Relative Prices — the Signal Buyers Actually Read

questions.question: Chicken costs R70/kg and beef R140/kg. The relative price of chicken in terms of beef is:
options: Half a kilogram of beef per kilogram of chicken
Two kilograms of beef per kilogram of chicken

questions.question: If ALL prices and all incomes double overnight, rational shoppers' choices between goods will:
options: Stay the same, because no relative price changed

questions.question: Beef doubles in price while chicken's price is unchanged. Chicken has become:
options: Relatively cheaper, even though its money price never moved

questions.question: A change in the price of a RELATED good causes, in our good's market:
options: A movement along the demand curve
A movement along the supply curve only
A shift of the entire demand curve

subtopics.title: Substitutes and Complements — and Their Graphs in Words

questions.question: Which pair are complements?
Chicken's price rises from R70 to R95 after a bird-flu outbreak. In the BEEF market, the demand curve:
options: Stays fixed while quantity moves along it

questions.question: If the price of cars rises, the demand curve for petrol:
options: Shifts right, because petrol is a substitute for cars
Is unaffected — different markets never interact
Shifts left, because cars and petrol are complements

questions.question: The symmetry rule states that for substitutes, the related good's price and our good's demand move:

subtopics.title: Product Markets and Factor Markets — the Loop That Connects Shops to Jobs

questions.question: The demand for bricklayers is called DERIVED demand because it:
options: Comes second-hand from the demand for houses

questions.question: Which is a FACTOR market?
options: The labour market where wages are set

questions.question: A housing boom in Gauteng most directly causes, in factor markets:
options: Higher demand for bricklayers, cement and finance

questions.question: The backward direction of the loop: higher wages and material costs cause product-market supply curves to:
options: Shift left, pushing product prices up

subtopics.title: The Four Market Structures — a First Map

questions.question: Very many small sellers, identical products, free entry, price-taking behaviour. This describes:
South Africa's mobile networks — a few large firms, difficult entry, each watching rivals' moves — are an example of:
The feature that separates monopolistic competition from perfect competition is:
options: Differentiated products giving each seller slight price power

questions.question: Which statement about classification is correct?
options: All four structures are perfect markets
Monopoly is the only perfect market
Only perfect competition is a perfect market; the other three are imperfect
Oligopoly and monopoly are perfect; the rest imperfect

subtopics.title: The Fridge Decides — Chicken, Beef and the Compared Price

questions.question: Braai packs and charcoal are:
options: Substitutes — rivals doing the same job

questions.question: When chicken jumps to R95, beef sales rise even though beef's price never moved. On beef's graph this appears as:
options: The whole demand curve stepping to the right
A slide down the existing demand curve

questions.question: The pocket rule from this section is:
options: Partners move together; rivals move apart
Rivals move together; partners move apart

subtopics.title: Every Job Is Hiding Inside Something Somebody Buys

questions.question: A bricklayer has a job ultimately because:
options: The government requires houses to be built
Somebody wants a house — labour demand is borrowed from product demand

questions.question: During the building spree, artisan wages get bid up because:
options: A new minimum wage was announced
Sites compete for scarce artisans as product demand spills into the labour market

questions.question: The bricklayer's higher pay 'pulls back' on product markets by:
options: Reducing the supply of houses to zero
Leaving the economy as savings only
Becoming household spending at the shops, via the circular flow

subtopics.title: Count the Sellers — From the Taxi Rank to the Grid

questions.question: The takeaways along one taxi route — many sellers, easy entry, each slightly different — form:
The bread price-fixing scandal is the lesson's example of:
The electricity grid past your house is a monopoly mainly because:
options: No rival can feasibly build a second grid, so entry is blocked

questions.question: The ladder rule of price power says: as sellers get fewer and entry gets harder, sellers move from:
options: Taking the price, to nudging it, to watching rivals, to making it
